This online appendix contains supplementary material referenced in the main paper. Specifically,
it includes: (i) the experimental instructions for both the laboratory and the survey experiments (Appendix A);
(ii) detailed explanations, along with the Python code, of how the main AI-related measures used in the analysis,
i.e., Idea request, Idea request index, and Similarity, have been constructed (Appendix B); and (iii) additional
results obtained by replicating the analysis in Section 4.3 of the paper based on the behavioral indicators of AI
reliance introduced by Zhu and Zou (2026), i.e., AI-first keywords and User-first keywords (Appendix C).

statements.quote:
This appendix describes the code used to construct the measures of Idea request, Idea request index, and
Similarity employed in the empirical analysis. The code is implemented in Python and operates directly on
the original experimental dataset containing participant writing and complete dialogue logs.
statements.locator: PDF p. 35 (Online Appendix p. 6), Appendix B, introductory paragraph.

statements.quote:
The code reconstructs each participant’s interaction with the AI using the
ordered sequence of participant queries (query_1 through query_19) and corresponding AI responses
(chat_response_1 through chat_response_19). Text fields may be empty. In the code, text is
minimally normalized by trimming whitespace and converting missing values to empty strings.
statements.locator: PDF p. 35 (Online Appendix p. 6), Appendix B.1, input dataset and dialogue fields.

statements.quote:
All constructed variables are deterministic functions of the observed dialogue logs, the final writing, and
a fixed API prompt and model specification. Given the same input dataset and API environment, the code
reproduces the AI involvement measures.
statements.locator: PDF p. 35 (Online Appendix p. 6), Appendix B.1, reproducibility statement.

what_we_could_compute: For final.open_items[4] (additional treatment-effect statistics), calculate analyzed counts, arm means, sample SDs, and SEs for S1-O1 creativity (grade_mean), S1-O2 character count (n_characters), and S1-O3 DAT score (dat_score), separately for the six arms and pooled AI versus No AI. All three outcomes have 360 observed participant values.

Recompute every participant creativity mean from grade_1 through grade_4 in Mendeley v2, then compute arm contrasts, confidence intervals, and standardized treatment effects. The four-rating row means were checked and exactly reproduce grade_mean.

Compute across-participant diversity/homogenization of the final compositions using writing linked to id_code and treatment, including arm-specific text similarities or embedding-based diversity. The raw texts support new measures; the existing sim_writing_ai_concat variable measures a participant versus their own AI responses, not diversity across participants.

For final.open_items[1], the 21 session identifiers permit session-clustered SE or resampling sensitivity analyses. Every observed session has a single treatment. The allocation protocol is still absent, so these data do not by themselves establish the randomization unit or which clustering is required.

For final.open_items[4], the newer Mendeley v2 script and individual ratings also permit peak-creativity outcomes (maximum of the four ratings) and its specified quantile regressions, which are additional analyses outside the saved PDF.
